[switching to stan-dev now that Jonah's on board]

You need to include

#include <boost/random/additive_combine.hpp> // L'Ecuyer RNG

and then you can instantiate the same way as stan/common/command.hpp:

typedef boost::ecuyer1988 rng_t; // (2**50 = 1T samples, 1000 chains)

unsigned int seed = ...;

rng_t base_rng(seed);

I really don't think hacking the CPP file is going to be
a good long-term solution because such a thing is very hard
to maintain.

I'd suggest that rather than changing the generated C++ code,
you add a wrapper function that calls it if you must. It'll be
much more robust to minor formatting changes and whatnot.

- Bob

On Monday, February 16, 2015 at 3:41:55 AM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I really don't think hacking the CPP file is going to be
a good long-term solution because such a thing is very hard
to maintain.  

I'd suggest that rather than changing the generated C++ code,
you add a wrapper function that calls it if you must.  It'll be
much more robust to minor formatting changes and whatnot.

The (or at least a) issue is that the sourceCpp() function in Rcpp can only export designated functions from the global namespace of a .cpp file. So, I even had to unwrap it from temporary model namespace and move all the using:: statements inside the functions. Thus, I can't otherwise see how to make it so that a user can call

foo()

from R and execute the foo() they defined in their .stan program.

Ben
